newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HRW wheat ratings steady but dryness a worry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HRW wheat ratings steady but dryness a worry.

text.p: Hard red winter wheat ratings were mostly steady for major producing states in the week ended May 18 but dryness continued to hit ratings in western Kansas and Nebraska, according to weekly crop reports issued by state agricultural statistics services.
KANSAS - Condition of the winter wheat were nearly unchanged from last week with the crop rated 11 percent excellent, 44 good, 30 fair, 11 poor and four very poor.

Topsoil moisture continued to decline statewide with 44 percent rated short to very short versus 23 pct last week. The NW district was rated 52 pct very short and 41 pct short, with the west and central districts also 45-50 pct short.
In Kansas, there were scattered reports of Russian wheat aphids and greenbugs in wheat. Wheat streak mosaic and leaf rust were also cited in some county reports.
Kansas wheat was 56 pct headed, level with last year but behind the 61 pct 5-year average. One percent had colored.

NEBRASKA - Wheat crop ratings fell sharply to 40 percent good to excellent, versus 56 percent at that level last week. The crop was rated 44 percent fair vs 38 pct last week and 16 percent poor to very poor, versus 8 percent a week ago.
Wheat was jointed 63 pct vs 44 a week ago, 68 year ago, 84 on a 5-year average. Wheat headed 1 pct vs 1 pct a year ago and 10 percent on the 5-year average.
Dryness was a growing concern for Nebraska wheat. "Southwestern wheat fields are in dire need of moisture," the weekly state crop report said.

The impact of a cold snap on May 13 was not yet clear. "The effects of last week's freezing temperatures were still being evaluated. Much of the panhandle crop had not yet jointed at the time of the freeze," the report said.

OKLAHOMA - The wheat crop made significant progress toward maturation in above normal temperatures and gusty winds. But foliar diseases were increasing in some counties and were reaching threshold levels in spots, the weekly report said.
Oklahoma wheat was rated 11 percent very poor, 18 poor, 35 fair, 34 good and 2 excellent. Wheat was 95 percent headed, versus 99 last year and 95 on the five-year average.
Cool evening temperatures benefited grain fill on late wheat, the weekly state crop report said.

TEXAS - Wheat conditions improved over much of the state with the crop rated 65 percent of normal versus 27 pct at the same time last year. Wheat was 1 percent harvested versus 2 last year and on average, with the crop 80 percent headed versus 89 last year and 85 on the 5-year average.

Harvest was increasing into central areas as weather allowed. Fields in the Blacklands and North Central districts were turning color as harvest neared. There were scattered reports of lodging. But fields in the High Plains where freeze damage was light were beginning to show good development and heading continued, the weekly state crop report said.
